newsitem.title: USA: 1997 outlook positive for emerging markets - MFS.
newsitem.headline: 1997 outlook positive for emerging markets - MFS.

text.p: The 1997 investment outlook for emerging markets is positive, said a portfolio manager for a large U.S. mutual fund family.

David Mannheim, vice president at MFS Investment Management, a Boston, Mass.-based group directing about $51.0 billion in investment funds, told the year-end MFS Investment Outlook meeting the long-term growth story for emerging markets was intact.
He noted, though, that the performances of these markets can be individualized, creating "significant performance differences" and a strong case for diversification.
Mannheim said MFS Investment Management's emerging market portfolios are "overweighted" in Brazil and the smaller countries of Latin America.
In Eastern Europe, valuations are "very compelling" in Poland, he said. In Asia, China, Hong Kong and India are overweighted, he said.

Mannheim said the MFS Investment Management's international and emerging market portfolios are underweighted in areas like energy, utilities and telecommunication. The latter area is experiencing "sub-par" earnings growth and a lot of competition, he said.
Companies focusing on metals, paper and other commodities are also underweighted because economic growth will probably not be strong enough to push commodities prices higher, Mannheim said.
The 1997 outlook for international equities in most developed countries is "generally positive," he said.

In Europe, Mannheim said he sees attractive relative valuations, improving corporate earnings growth and opportunities among companies that are steady earners, that have multinational markets or are in special situations.
Mannheim said he was overweighted in Sweden and Britain.
